metaTitle: Zoom for Animators on Mac: Screen Share and Reviews
description: Use Zoom for animators on Mac for directing calls and shot reviews. Share at full quality, avoid the 720p cap, and ask Lazur for help mid-call.

intro: Zoom for animators on Mac is the live room for directing calls, shot reviews and quick notes. Zoom handles the talk and the screen share. Frame-level marks usually belong in a separate review tool. This page covers the Mac settings that matter for animation, the limits you will hit, and where Lazur fits in. Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch of your Mac.
tldr: Turn on Optimize Share for Full-screen Video Clip for motion, and play the clip full screen before you share.
A virtual background without a green screen caps your outgoing video at 720p on Zoom.
Free Zoom meetings end at 40 minutes, so plan long reviews around that limit.
Keep frame notes in a review tool. Use Zoom for the talk around them.
Hold ⌥⌘ to ask Lazur where a control is. Hold fn to dictate a note at the cursor.

blocks.text: What animators actually do on Zoom

Most animators use Zoom for the talk around the work, not the frames themselves. Directing calls, dailies, comp check-ins and pitch sessions all happen on video. The shots get reviewed in a tool built for frames.

Blue Zoo, a UK animation studio, says its direction now runs over Zoom. The studio's animation director says animators can drop in and out of group reviews and keep working in the background. That removes the wait between a note and the next fix.

The lighting and compositing supervisor at the same studio says remote review lets the director pause, highlight and discuss a note faster than a single-monitor room allows. That speed comes from sharing one screen with the people who need to see it.
Typical Zoom calls in an animation team

items: Live direction, where the director watches a playblast and talks through timing.
Dailies, where the team reviews yesterday's shots and logs notes.
Lighting and comp checks, where a supervisor marks a problem on a shared frame.
Pitch and boarding calls, where you walk through storyboards beat by beat.
Quick syncs, where one shot gets a fix, an owner and a deadline.

blocks.text: Set up your Mac before the call starts

Start with permissions. Zoom needs permission to record your screen before it can share it. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, then switch Zoom on. Quit and reopen Zoom if the share still shows a blank window.
Menu names can shift between macOS versions. If your screen differs, search System Settings for Screen Recording.

Next, control what the room sees. Quit chat apps and mail you do not need for the call. Turn on a Focus, such as Do Not Disturb, from Control Center. A banner from a chat app during a playblast is the fastest way to lose a room.
A pre-call checklist for animation reviews

items: Open the exact file and pause on the first frame you will show.
Test a short share with the producer before the real call starts.
Turn off the virtual background unless you use a green screen.
Close browser tabs you do not need, so playback stays smooth.
Keep a phone dial-in number ready in case the connection drops.

blocks.text: CGWire's feedback guide says internet drops, software bugs and hardware crashes can halt a review in seconds. A phone dial-in is cheap insurance for that moment.
Share animation at full quality on Zoom

Screen sharing compresses what you show, and motion suffers most. Zoom has a setting for moving clips. During a share, click More in the screen share controls and turn on Optimize Share for Full-screen Video Clip. Turn it on only when the clip moves.
A university IT guide makes the same point. Check the option for full-screen video clips, and leave it off otherwise, because the shared screen can turn blurry.
Play the clip full screen on your Mac before you start the share. A small player window inside a big desktop gives the setting less to work with. Then share that window or the full screen.

blocks.text: Computer sound is the risky one. It goes to everyone on the call, not only the person you are talking to. Share it only when the room needs to hear the clip, and use headphones for anything else.
Video limits that change what the room sees

Zoom's virtual background has a limit that catches people off guard. Without a green screen, Zoom caps outgoing video at 720p. Zoom's support article lists this cap for virtual backgrounds. While the background is on, your camera feed stays at 720p.

Full 1080p with a virtual background and no green screen needs more hardware. Zoom lists an Apple M-series MacBook Pro as one option. Check the requirements page before a review where the camera picture matters.
Most animation reviews do not need the background at all. Turn it off for reviews, unless the background matters to the call.

Zoom also lists a 60 FPS screen share for motion-heavy content. It comes through the Enhanced Media add-on for Meetings and Rooms. Ask the account owner whether your plan includes it before you plan a motion review around it.
Meeting length and participant limits on Zoom

blocks.caption: Zoom meeting limits as listed on Zoom's pricing page.

blocks.text: Zoom's pricing FAQ says all plans allow up to 100 participants by default. The Large Meeting add-on raises that limit to 1,000.

blocks.title: Free plan limit
blocks.text: Basic meetings end at 40 minutes. Save your notes in a review tool as you go, so nothing is lost when the call closes.
A review that runs an hour will end partway through on a free plan. Plan the split before the call starts. Ask Lazur to set a timer for when the limit is near.
Keep frame notes in a review tool, not the call

Zoom is good at talk. It is weak at marks. A frame number said out loud is gone by the next shot. CGWire's guide suggests leaving comments on specific frames, so the artist can respond later while reviewers keep working.

CGWire also points to Kitsu's sync review. People watch the same animation together and comment in real time. Educational Voice names Frame.io, SyncSketch and StudioBinder for reviews and annotations, and Miro and Figma for shared boards.
Pick one review tool for the whole team, not one per call. Use Zoom to explain a note. Use the review tool to record it. Say the frame, then add the note where the shot lives.

items: The shot name and the frame number.
What you see, described without guessing the animator's intent.
The change you want, in one sentence.
Whether it is a timing, pose or lighting note.
An owner and a day for the fix.

blocks.text: Dictate notes and draft replies during the call

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You can dictate into a review tool open in a browser beside Zoom, or into a note in your notes app. Dictation is unlimited on Pro and Power.
Lazur's personal dictionary helps with animation terms. Add words like squash and stretch or overlap, so they land spelled right.
Snippets and clipboard slots handle repeat work. Save a note template as a snippet. Keep a clipboard slot for the shot names you type all day.
When a director writes in chat during the call, ask Lazur to draft a reply. Read the draft, edit it, then send it yourself. Lazur drafts the text. You still press send.
Ask Lazur about the screen without leaving Zoom
Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. It looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut, so it is not watching the call the rest of the time.
Ask where something is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask where More is in the share controls, and Lazur circles it. You click it yourself.
Ask how to do something and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click. That is slower than a shortcut, but it helps when you do not know a control panel well.
Mind the speaker. Lazur's answer comes out loud. If computer sound is shared, the room can hear it. Use headphones during a share, or ask your question before you start sharing.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. Think of it as a guide that points. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
For a deeper walkthrough, read [Zoom for Mac with Lazur](/apps/zoom).
Common mistakes animators make on Zoom
Mistake one: sharing the whole desktop. Chat banners, private windows and a folder full of drafts all reach the room. Share one window when you can.
Mistake two: leaving the virtual background on. The camera drops to 720p, and the picture looks softer than it should.
Mistake three: forgetting the free plan limit. The meeting ends at 40 minutes, and the notes you were typing end with it. Save notes as you go.
Mistake four: giving notes only out loud. Spoken notes get lost by the next shot. Log each one with its frame number before you move on.
Mistake five: skipping the audio check. Test computer sound before the call, so the clip and the room hear the same thing.
Where remote review works and where it does not
Blue Zoo says some parts of its pipeline do not suit Zoom meetings or messages sent later. Its co-founder, Tom Box, says staff miss the personal side of collaboration.
That matters for animators. Some notes need a room, a shared wall or a long look at a character. Plan one in-person or small-group check on a regular basis, even for a fully remote team.
What the survey numbers do and do not tell you

The clearest numbers come from Frame.io. A 2020 survey of nearly 600 people, mostly post-production professionals, found 73% were equally or more productive working remotely. The same survey found 65% reported better work-life balance.
Treat those figures with care. The survey is from 2020, and it covers post-production, not animation alone. It does not measure Zoom. It does suggest remote review works when the tools fit the job.
A review routine for one shot

items: Export a playblast and open it full screen on the Mac.
Turn Focus on and quit chat apps.
Turn off the virtual background.
Share the window, with full-screen clip optimization on if the shot moves.
Walk the room through the shot once, pausing on the key frames.
Log each note in the review tool with its frame number.
Read the list back, and confirm an owner and a day for every fix.

blocks.text: Keep the routine short. A review that runs long on a free plan ends on its own, and the last notes never get logged.
Getting started with Lazur on your Mac
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Start with the free trial. It needs no credit card, and it starts the first time you open the app.
Pro and Power list their prices and AI action limits on the [pricing page](/pricing). Check the current details there before you choose a plan.
Download Lazur from the [download page](/download), then open it once. Hold ⌥⌘ during a Zoom call and ask where the share button is.
For frame work outside Zoom, see [Photoshop for animators on Mac](/for/animators/photoshop) and [Chrome for animators on Mac](/for/animators/chrome).

faq.question: Does Zoom work well for animation reviews on Mac?
faq.answer: Zoom works well for live direction and talk around the work. Frame-level notes belong in a review tool such as Frame.io, SyncSketch or Kitsu. Use Zoom to explain a note, then record it where the shot lives.

faq.question: Why does my animation look blurry when I share it on Zoom?
faq.answer: Motion and small windows cause most of the blur. Play the clip full screen, then turn on Optimize Share for Full-screen Video Clip in the More menu of the share controls. Switch that option off for still frames, because it can blur them.

faq.question: Can I run a long director review on a free Zoom account?
faq.answer: Not for long. Zoom's free Basic plan ends meetings at 40 minutes and allows up to 100 participants. Zoom lists Pro at 30 hours. Split long reviews into two calls, or move the review to a paid plan.

faq.question: Why is my camera stuck at 720p during a Zoom call?
faq.answer: A virtual background without a green screen caps outgoing video at 720p. Turn the background off for reviews. Zoom lists 1080p with a background and no green screen as needing more hardware, such as an Apple M-series MacBook Pro.

faq.question: How do I share computer sound without sending alerts to everyone?
faq.answer: You cannot limit computer sound to one person. It plays to all participants. Turn on a Focus before you share, quit chat apps, and share computer sound only when the room needs the clip audio.

faq.question: Can Lazur click through Zoom for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It can circle the control, label it, and guide you one click at a time while it waits for each click.

faq.question: Does Lazur watch my screen during the whole call?
faq.answer: No. Lazur looks at the screen only while you hold ⌥⌘. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Is Lazur available on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.
